audit_findings.title: Affiliate earnings may be capitalized twice
audit_findings.magnitude: $4.143 billion bridge amount and $648 million of 2025 affiliate earnings; exact overlap unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Affiliate earnings enter recurring OE while the corresponding investments are separately added through stakes_net.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company’s proportionate share of the net income or loss of these investees is included in consolidated net earnings.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that consolidated earnings include ADM's share of affiliate income, but the supplied record does not demonstrate whether those earnings were removed from OE. If they remain, the model capitalizes both the earnings stream and the $4.143 billion stake value. That would be a material overstatement, although the error itself remains unresolved pending the OE reconciliation.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every OE year to GAAP earnings, remove earnings and losses attributable to every investment included in stakes_net with consistent tax treatment, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The portfolio-income purge may capture operating economics and investment losses
audit_findings.magnitude: $118 million 2025 net income line containing $372 million of revaluation losses; exact correction unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The purge changes OE by removing some combination of operating interest income, investment income, and investment revaluation gains or losses.
audit_findings.evidence: Interest and investment income decreased $444 million to $118 million, primarily due to revaluation losses of $372 million, driven by $257 million and $115 million within Corporate and the Nutrition segment, respectively, in addition to lower interest income at ADM Investor Services due to lower interest rates.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that one account combines materially different economics. The $372 million revaluation loss alone equals 49.3% of the $754.2 million anchor, so an account-level classification error is reasonably capable of materially changing OE. The record does not demonstrate which components were actually purged, so the existence and direction of a valuation error remain unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the account-level OE workpaper, retain ADM Investor Services operating economics, match investment income and revaluation results to the assets included in the bridge, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The latest-year anchor may be dominated by nonrecurring items
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.251 billion gross listed items; $743 million net listed losses over gain before tax, equal to 98.5% of the $754.2 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: One-time gains and losses affect the 2025 OE anchor, which drives every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2025, the Company recorded $372 million of impairments driven by revaluation losses related to investments in the alternative protein market and the Company's updated investment strategy around startup and development stage companies, $283 million of asset impairment, exit, contingency, restructuring charges, and impairment charges of $179 million related to previously capitalized software, and Wilmar International Limited (“Wilmar”) equity earnings related impacts reflecting a one time remeasurement gain of $254 million and a $163 million penalty charge.
audit_findings.explanation: The listed items are nearly equal to the entire anchor on a net pre-tax basis, making the valuation highly sensitive to their treatment. This does not demonstrate that the anchor is wrong because impairments, restructuring costs, investment losses, taxes, and the Wilmar gain may already receive different OE adjustments. It does demonstrate material normalization risk in both directions.
audit_findings.action: Tie each listed item to the 2025 OE calculation, document a symmetric cash-versus-noncash and recurring-versus-nonrecurring policy, apply related taxes consistently, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Material litigation exposure is not visibly captured
audit_findings.magnitude: $500 million to over $2.0 billion alleged damages, equivalent to $1.02 to over $4.10 per diluted share and approximately 2.9% to 15.1% of scenario equity values
audit_findings.mechanism: Any uninsured settlement or judgment would reduce the equity bridge or future OE through cash payments and legal costs.
audit_findings.evidence: AOT and Maize allege that members of the putative class collectively suffered damages calculated to be between approximately $ 500 million to over $ 2.0 billion as a result of the Company’s alleged actions.
audit_findings.explanation: The damages range is a claimant allegation, not a demonstrated liability, and the filings do not establish probability, insurance recovery, or a reasonably estimable loss. Nevertheless, the disclosed range is large enough relative to the $13.262-$17.069 billion scenario equity values to be materially value-relevant. The June 2026 filing shows some related dismissals but continues to disclose unresolved proceedings.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile existing legal reserves, insurance and indemnification coverage to the bridge and OE; obtain post-quarter case developments and counsel's probability assessment; then run probability-weighted and stated-range downside cases.

audit_findings.title: Redeemable NCI is a claim outside owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $292 million at June 30, 2026, or $0.60 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: The temporary-equity redemption claim should reduce the equity bridge because its redemption-value changes bypass OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company presents any redeemable non-controlling interests in temporary equity within the Consolidated Balance Sheets at redemption value with period changes recorded in reinvested earnings.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filed claim is $292 million. If entirely omitted, deducting it would reduce the scenario values from $27.18-$34.98 to approximately $26.58-$34.38 per share, still 59.4%-68.6% below the $84.61 market price. It is therefore a demonstrated bridge issue if not already netted elsewhere, but not material to the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Verify that the $292 million is not included in stakes_net or another bridge account, deduct it if absent, and document the redemption terms and latest balance.

audit_findings.title: The PSU share ceiling is not proven to cover maximum settlement
audit_findings.mechanism: Shares issued above one share per reported PSU would increase the fully diluted denominator and reduce value per share.
audit_findings.evidence: The awards for PSUs are made in common stock units and vest at the end of a vesting period of three years subject to the attainment of certain future service and Company performance criteria.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing reports 5.398 million combined nonvested restricted awards and PSUs, equal to 1.1% of the 487.953 million-share denominator, but it does not separate PSUs or disclose their maximum payout multiplier. Missing dilution is therefore possible, but the record cannot establish its size or materiality. Retaining compensation expense does not replace the missing shares.
audit_findings.action: Review the 2026 proxy, amended incentive plan, and award agreements for PSU counts and maximum payout multipliers; add only the excess maximum-settlement shares to the denominator and rerun per-share values.
